drop.reason: Resource paper: the result is a set of new drosophilid genome assemblies and the sequencing approach, not an evolutionary finding.
Single-species genome assembly; the allopolyploidization history is secondary and polyploidy is already covered by Poaceae and Sonneratia papers.
Within-species centromere mapping in soybean; centromere biology more than molecular evolution, below the cut.
Human mtDNA disease study; 'purifying selection' is somatic selection across a patient's immune cells, not genome evolution.
Cancer genomics (colitis-associated cancer drivers); tumour evolution belongs to cancergen.
Within-patient pathogen adaptation is already represented by the S. aureus paper; this one centres on a clinical phenotypic switch.
16S amplicon microbial ecology; the speciation claim rests on community data, weak molecular-evolution content.
Mainly metabolic physiology of syntrophic partners from metagenomes; the evolutionary result is secondary.
Simulation study of inference bias for malaria surveillance; methodological, below the cut.
Structural modelling of peptide-receptor binding; coevolution is used as a tool, not the finding.
Biogeography of phylogenetic turnover; not about how genomes or genes evolve.
Mitogenome assembly with descriptive comparisons; mostly a resource.
Single-nucleus neurobiology of a behaviour; uses evolutionary vocabulary only.
Near-duplicate in kind: prokaryote salinity adaptation via phylogenomics is already kept (aquatic bacteria, 37235649).
Plant immune receptor identification; convergent evolution is secondary to functional immunology.
Single-species genome paper; WGD and C4 trait evolution fit evodevo better and polyploidy is covered.
Methods paper (single-worm amplification and long-read sequencing).

notes: The kept set covers deep and shallow phylogenomics (mammals, eukaryotes, nematodes, birds), incomplete lineage sorting and hybrid speciation, selection scans and linked selection in humans, plants, insects and microbiomes, genome structural evolution (fusions, inversions, SVs, rearrangements), whole-genome duplication, horizontal gene transfer, orphan genes, ancient DNA and experimental evolution. It is weighted toward plants, animals and microbes in leading journals. It is thin on viral evolution (one coronavirus paper), on theory and methods, and on non-human population genetics outside crops and pests.
